programme.title: The Story of Scottish Art
programme.desc: Artist Lachlan Goudie celebrates the impact of Scottish art on the international art world, covering 5,000 years from the early Neolithic age to the present day. The first edition explores rock markings at Kilmartin Glen and the oldest sculpted human figure in the British Isles, as well as the illuminated pages of the Book of Kells. The artist also examines art found in churches, including a painting of the Crucifixion dating from the late 1400s

programme.title: Alaska: Earth's Frozen Kingdom
programme.desc: Documentary following the fortunes of humans and animals over the course of a year in Alaska, which is by far the biggest US state and still one of the wildest places on Earth with deep forests and vast mountain ranges. The arrival of spring sees Alaska go through a huge transformation as water, light and warmth return, with animals emerging from hibernation and rushing to cash in on the riches of the season. Dougray Scott narrates

programme.title: An Art Lovers' Guide
programme.desc: Historian Janina Ramirez and art critic Alastair Sooke embark on cultural city breaks, offering insights into the most famous locations and uncovering hidden gems and untold stories to reveal how religion, revolution and trailblazing individuals can shape the art - and soul - of a metropolis. They begin by examining the art and design of the Dutch capital Amsterdam, along the way discovering how its culture reflects the liberal attitudes, appetite for global trade and love of home comforts that helped shape the character of this city

programme.title: Secrets of Skin
programme.desc: Biologist Ben Garrod examines how animals use their skin to send out messages to their own species, and warning signals to others, from vibrant displays of colour to skin pouches to amplify sounds

programme.title: Weatherman Walking
programme.sub-title: Weatherman Walking: Dylan's Walks - Swansea & Llansteffan
programme.desc: In the first of two special programmes originally shown to celebrate the centenary of Dylan Thomas's birth, Derek Brockway strolls around the poet's home town of Swansea. Accompanied by actor Adrian Metcalfe, Derek sets off from Dylan's childhood home on Cwmdonkin Drive and walks through the city's parks and down to the seafront, before visiting some of the writer's haunts in later life. He then heads west to the Llansteffan peninsula where his guide, artist Osi Rhys Osmond, leads him through the countryside that was home to many of Dylan's relatives. They include his aunt's farm, which would provide the inspiration for the poem Fernhill

programme.title: To the Manor Born
programme.desc: Audrey leads locals in a rally against the proposed closure of the village's railway station, while DeVere harbours plans to build a new supermarket on the site. Comedy, guest starring Richard Thorp

programme.title: Keeping Up Appearances
programme.desc: Hyacinth attends an exclusive auction, while Daisy and Rose try to cool the ardour of a woman who seems determined to marry Daddy. Comedy, starring Patricia Routledge, Judy Cornwell and Josephine Tewson

programme.title: The Normans
programme.desc: Professor Robert Bartlett examines the Normans' expansion towards southern Europe and the Middle East in the 11th century. Southern Italy and Sicily were conquered and a prosperous kingdom flourished on the island, which became an important centre of medieval culture and an example of harmony between religions. However, Pope Urban II's call for holy war against the Muslims, to win Jerusalem back, led to the Normans embarking on the First Crusade

programme.title: Storyville
programme.desc: Syrian filmmakers Hasan Kattan and Fadi Al-Halabi navigate the reality of the UK asylum system, documenting a new chapter in their own lives shaped by uncertainty, bureaucracy and displacement. Their experiences offer an intimate perspective on life in exile and the enduring power of storytelling in the face of adversity

programme.title: Storyville
programme.desc: Vladimir Kara-Murza is a Russian opposition politician and journalist who survived two near-fatal poisonings before being sentenced to 25 years in prison after speaking out against Russia's invasion of Ukraine. In this documentary, cameras follow his wife Evgenia Kara-Murza during his imprisonment as she mounts a global campaign to bring him home and ensure that his voice will not be silenced

programme.title: Secrets of Size: Atoms to Supergalaxies
programme.desc: Part one of two. Jim Al-Khalili explores the universe at the smallest scales, from tiny atoms to vast galaxies. The first episode examines objects too small to glimpse with the naked eye, and reveals how nanomaterials such as graphene are revolutionising engineering, medicine, computing, electronics and environmental science

programme.title: Secrets of Skin
programme.desc: Biologist Ben Garrod explores the complex ways, from camouflage to deadly toxins, in which the skin helps animals defend themselves against threats of all kinds. Featuring a look at one of the most iconic warnings in nature - that of the rattlesnake. Ben takes a teaching sample of a rattlesnake's tail to the University of Bristol to test just how fast in can vibrate

programme.title: Weatherman Walking
programme.sub-title: Weatherman Walking: Dylan's Walks - New Quay and Laugharne
programme.desc: Derek Brockway presents the second of two specials originally shown to celebrate the centenary of Dylan Thomas's birth. First he travels to the seaside town of New Quay on Cardigan Bay, where the poet and writer lived with wife Caitlin during the Second World War. Jeff Towns, chairman of the Dylan Thomas Society, joins Derek to explain how Thomas was inspired to write some of his greatest work during this era. For his final walk, to Laugharne, the presenter is accompanied by Thomas's grandaughter Hannah Ellis, who reveals the significance of the town to both her grandparents and her family today

programme.title: What Are UFOs?
programme.desc: For decades, UFOs have intrigued the world, but many scientists avoided studying them. In the US, after highly publicised sightings of unidentified objects by US Navy pilots, UFOs are moving out of the shadows and into the light as NASA pledges to study them scientifically. This programme follows astrophysicists and engineers using new technologies to investigate strange objects in the sky

programme.title: Building Sights
programme.desc: Architect Norman Foster takes a look at the jumbo jet. First broadcast September 9, 1991

programme.title: Television's Opening Night: How the Box Was Born
programme.desc: Dallas Campbell, Professor Danielle George and Dr Hugh Hunt mark the 80th anniversary of Britain's very first TV broadcast by trying to recreate the landmark event. The inaugural programme came live from Alexandria Palace on November 2, 1936, but there are no surviving recordings of the show. In response, the presenter trio set out to recreate every aspect of this first broadcast, from the variety acts featured right down to the camera equipment used, using authentic technology and filming techniques. Plus, pioneering TV engineer John Logie Baird's assistant - now aged 104 - is on hand to lend some technical assistance, and Dallas meets one of the performers who appeared on the first programme to find out what it is like to be part of TV history

programme.title: The Fools on the Hill
programme.desc: Jack Rosenthal's 1986 drama based on the BBC's first 'high-definition' television broadcast at London's Alexandra Palace on November 2, 1936. The service was set to be the first of its kind in the world - but behind the scenes, not everything was going to plan. Starring Shaughan Seymour

programme.title: Television Comes to London
programme.desc: A look at how television came to Alexandra Palace, with an insight into production routine. Featuring many behind-the-scenes shots, such as a sequence showing Adele Dixon appearing to viewers in the Variety, which then reveals the technical staff and equipment in the studio that made this transmission possible. First broadcast November 2, 1936

programme.title: John Logie Baird: The Man Who Saw the Future
programme.desc: The story of the inventor and electrical engineer, who was the first person to give a successful public demonstration of television. The programme includes rare archive footage and offers a fascinating insight into a man who was totally committed to his work, miraculously surviving a 1,000-volt electric shock during one of his early experiments

programme.title: The Birth of Television
programme.desc: Leslie Mitchell announced the official opening of the first high-definition public television service in the world on November 2 1936. Forty years later, from the same studio at Alexandra Palace, he traces the origins of television from the beginning of this century to the first outside broadcast - the coronation of George VI in May 1937. First broadcast in 1976

Their three-bedroom chalet bungalow has been bursting at the seams since the arrival of their two children - and the mountains of toys and chaos they bring. programme.title: Jason Bourne (2016)
programme.desc: Former government operative Jason Bourne has been in hiding for 12 years after exposing a sinister CIA operation. However, he once again finds himself being hunted down when a former CIA operative gone rogue acquires top secret information - including details of Bourne's own father's involvement in a clandestine scheme. Action thriller, starring Matt Damon, Tommy Lee Jones, Alicia Vikander and Julia Stiles

programme.title: The Bourne Identity (2002)
programme.desc: A fishing boat crew plucks a man out of the sea with two bullet wounds in his back and a safety-deposit number sewn into his skin - but absolutely no memory of who he is or how he got there. In the search for his true identity, he is pursued by assassins - but his skill at evading them suggests his own past is far from straightforward. Thriller, starring Matt Damon, Franka Potente, Chris Cooper, Clive Owen and Brian Cox

programme.title: The Bourne Supremacy (2004)
programme.desc: The amnesiac assassin is living quietly in hiding, until his former employers come after him again and murder his girlfriend. A CIA operation has ended in disaster, and those responsible intend to clear their names by implicating Bourne. As the former secret agent tries to evade the hitmen on his trail, he also struggles to piece together the truth about his past. Action thriller sequel, starring Matt Damon, Brian Cox, Joan Allen and Julia Stiles

programme.title: The Bourne Ultimatum (2007)
programme.desc: Amnesiac rogue assassin Jason Bourne's long-buried memories are reawakened by a British journalist researching the secret organisation that was responsible for transforming him into a killing machine. Meanwhile, a ruthless CIA director becomes convinced Bourne is still a security risk, and plans to dispose of him once and for all. Third instalment of the spy thriller series, directed by Paul Greengrass and starring Matt Damon, Joan Allen, Julia Stiles, David Strathairn, Paddy Considine, Scott Glenn and Albert Finney

programme.title: The Bourne Legacy (2012)
programme.desc: The leaders of a secret government agency plan to eliminate several agents as part of a cover-up when they face having their dark secrets exposed. One of the targets is able to evade his fate and go on the run - but his escape is threatened by his dependence on drugs to boost his physical and mental capabilities. Spy thriller sequel, with Jeremy Renner, Rachel Weisz and Edward Norton

Frances Barber, Kenneth Cranham and Dave Hill guest star

programme.title: Waking the Dead
programme.desc: Part one of two. When a skull is found buried in concrete in a church crypt, Boyd seeks to find out who it belongs to and why it is there, but gets little help from the Church authorities who seem bent on obscuring the facts. When another body is discovered the finger of guilt points to a workman, but why has a retired priest been so uncooperative and why is the corpse adorned with ritualistic symbols? Boyd resolves to solve the case and confront his own demons over the disappearance of his son at the same time. Trevor Eve and Sue Johnston star in a feature-length episode, with guest appearances by Annette Crosbie and Barry Morse

Trevor McDonald presents as investigators explore new leads in the infamous case of Fred and Rose West, suggesting there may be more victims than the 12 already known. programme.title: Killer Women with Piers Morgan
programme.desc: Journalist and TV personality Piers Morgan continues his travels across the USA, this time meeting two very different female murderers, both of whom killed someone they loved. First, he heads to Florida's largest female prison to visit Amanda Hutto, who is serving a life sentence for murdering her daughter. programme.title: Killer Women with Piers Morgan
programme.desc: Broadcaster and journalist Piers Morgan travels across the USA to meet some of America's most notorious female murderers, in a quest to discover what drives a woman to kill. He travels to Lowell Correctional Institute in Florida to talk to Rebecca Fenton, convicted for the murder of her husband Larry, who was shot dead in their home. programme.title: Great Continental Railway Journeys
programme.desc: Michael Portillo traces the early 20th-century roots of the Spanish Civil War, which divided his family and sent his father into exile. programme.title: Great Continental Railway Journeys
programme.desc: Michael Portillo travels from the chateaux of the Loire Valley to the heart of the Champagne region at Reims, beginning in the city of Orleans in north-central France. Here, he follows his Bradshaw's guide to the magnificent stained-glass windows of the Cathedral of Sainte-Croix, which tell the story of the heroine of France, Joan of Arc. Later, Michael takes a spin around the track at Le Mans in a French-built car, before making his way to the capital city of Paris. East of Paris, Michael finishes this leg of his journey in style with a tour of the cellars at Domaine Pommery in Reims

programme.title: Great Continental Railway Journeys
programme.desc: Michael Portillo ventures on a rail journey through Germany, guided by Bradshaw's Continental Railway Guide published in 1936. Starting in the vibrant city of Berlin, Michael visits the Museum of Modern Art in Berlin's Kreuzberg, where he sees how a leading artist of the era, George Grosz, warned of the rise of fascism in a haunting self-portrait. In the Schöneberg district of the capital, Michael researches the decadent night scene of the 1920s, and looks at how cabaret culture is being revived today. When he reaches Weimar, Michael investigates the beginnings of Bauhaus design and visits the movement's first building, before travelling onto Stuttgart, where he takes a ride in a high-performance Porsche to the manufacturer's Stuttgart headquarters
